title: Negligible current-induced torque from the bulk and interface of Al
authors: Taiyang Zhang, Lujun Zhu, Zhihao Yan, Lijun Zhu
abstract: The light metal Al was predicted to have strong orbital Hall and Rashba effects from its bulk and interface, respectively. In this letter, we report experimental evidence that neither the bulk nor the interface of the Al contributed a detectable torque on adjacent Co and FePt layers with significant spin Hall effect, spin-orbit coupling, and resistivity mismatch with Al. These results suggest minimal orbital-spin conversion in Al and negligible orbital transport and spin-vorticity torque in Co/Al, Al/Co, and Al/FePt bilayers. Our findings suggest poor generality and/or effectiveness of torque contributions by the orbital Hall effect, the interfacial orbital Rashba effect, and the spin-vorticity coupling.
summary: This work experimentally investigates whether Aluminum (Al) contributes significant torque via its bulk or interface when placed between magnetic layers like Co and FePt. By measuring harmonic Hall voltages, the authors report that these orbital contributions are negligible across varying Al thicknesses. This suggests that for these specific systems, other mechanisms dominate over predicted orbital-spin conversion effects in Al.
main_problem: To experimentally clarify the general effectiveness of orbital contributions (orbital Hall effect, interfacial orbital Rashba effect) to Spin-Orbit Torques (SOTs) in normal metal/ferromagnet heterostructures.
main_result: The study found that neither the bulk nor the interface of Aluminum (Al) contributed a detectable torque on adjacent magnetic layers like Co and FePt, suggesting minimal orbital-spin conversion in Al.
method: SOTs were quantified from angle-dependent harmonic Hall voltage measurements ($V_{2\omega}$) performed on fabricated Hall bar devices.
model_or_system: The research investigates spin-orbit torques in heterostructures involving light metal Aluminum (Al) interfaced with ferromagnetic metals such as Cobalt (Co) and FePt. The analysis contrasts established SHE-driven SOT mechanisms with predicted orbital contributions.
key_observables: Dampinglike ($\xi_{	ext{DL}}^E$) and fieldlike ($\xi_{	ext{FL}}^E$) Spin-Orbit Torque efficiencies, measured via $V_{2\omega}$ vs $\phi$ measurements.
important_parameters: Al thickness ($d_{	ext{Al}}$) varying from 0 nm to 4 nm; magnetic materials (Co, FePt).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on fitting the harmonic Hall voltage dependence on the in-plane magnetic field angle ($\phi$) to extract torque components.
figures_summary: Figures show $\xi_{	ext{DL}}^E$ and $\xi_{	ext{FL}}^E$ for various bilayers (Pt/Co/Al, FePt/Al, Al/Co) as a function of Al thickness, demonstrating the constancy or near-zero values across different thicknesses.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the scientific problem by contrasting theoretical predictions with experimental measurements. It details the measurement techniques using harmonic Hall voltage analysis on specific bilayers (e.g., $	ext{Pt}/	ext{Co}/	ext{Al}$ and $	ext{FePt}/	ext{Al}$) to quantify SOTs, leading to the conclusion of negligible torque contributions from Al.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter magnetism, the precise measurement and null result regarding orbital torques provide critical boundary conditions for theories describing spin-orbit coupling effects in novel material interfaces relevant to quantum spintronics devices.
